scope: Q25:B0 only; compared full question_text and visible_question, all four option texts/sections, and disclosed theory excerpt. No code executed.

options.label: A
options.facts: Wrong plausible model, but CME is not a typical race symptom and easy diagnosis is unsupported.
options.sections: Mostly consistent; claims 'race usually silent' too broadly, and 'CME is separate' requires qualification since CME itself can arise under unsynchronized interference.
options.finding: text: misleading symptom/frequency and guaranteed ease of diagnosis; sections: categorical distinction.

options.label: B
options.facts: False claim that volatile serializes access is a plausible visibility/atomicity confusion. Sections accurately refute it.
options.sections: Consistent; Atomic*/synchronization are suitable approaches depending on invariant.

options.label: C
options.facts: Definition and patterns are sound. Sections contain a false example: ConcurrentHashMap.get absent key returns null, not NPE; NPE requires later unboxing/dereference. computeIfAbsent is not a universal replacement. Theory corrects this example but does not repair option text.
options.sections: explanation is inconsistent with theory correction and says NPE 'на get'; remaining claims broadly sound.
options.finding: text omits how to fight race despite full question asking 'и как с ним бороться'; explanation gives a false NPE path.

options.label: D
options.facts: Plausible overclaim about immutability; wrong because shared mutable reference/container remains racy.
options.sections: what_actually/how_it_should_be mostly correct; source_of_confusion falsely says publication necessarily requires volatile/Atomic (safe publication has other means); if_it_were_true confuses atomic reference assignment with safe publication and invariant protection.
options.finding: sections: publication and atomic-reference claims overstate requirements; shared ref claim needs scoped explanation.

CONTENT.reason: Question asks definition and mitigation; every text is complete as a distractor except C gives no mitigation.

FACTS.reason: A's symptom claim; C's explanatory NPE claim; D section's safe-publication overclaim.

LINKAGE.reason: C explanation contains a broken ConcurrentHashMap example; D sections conflate atomic reference assignment and safe publication.

SECTIONS.reason: C explanation contradicts disclosed theory; A and D include categorical/overstated statements.

SFPL.reason: Visible MCQ uses abbreviated question 'Что такое Race Condition?', while JSON asks additionally how to combat it; options do not match that full scope.

ANSC.reason: A-D share the same definition lead-in and parallel parenthetical claim structure; C's extra pattern list remains comparable.

RU.reason: Mixed English/Russian technical prose is understandable, but D's 'снимают гонку' is awkward; several sections use categorical colloquial wording.

findings.label: A
findings.issue: CME is not generally a race-condition symptom; 'легко диагностируется' unsupported; CME is not wholly separate from concurrent interference.

findings.label: C
findings.issue: Does not answer mitigation part of full question_text.

findings.label: C
findings.issue: ConcurrentHashMap.get returns null for absent key; NPE is only downstream on unboxing/dereference.

findings.label: D
findings.issue: Safe publication is not limited to volatile/Atomic; atomic reference write alone does not establish safe publication.

sources.checked: JLS 17.4.5 happens-before; 17.7 non-atomic compound operations; volatile semantics.
get may overlap updates; absent mapping yields null; CME not thrown by CHM iterators; computeIfAbsent contract.
int may be updated atomically; atomic increment API.

limits: Primary Java 21 sources checked; no compile/runtime test, no review of other questions, no evidence workflow/record performed. These findings do not constitute FINAL or acceptance of the full file.
